key_gap: The AI independently converged to the same working design (2×54W headlight heaters, thermostat 37°C + independent 39.5°C cutoff, 100Ah battery, ≈$220) and correctly rejected solar-only on energy math — but reached it by opportunistic selection: it never enumerated the local element inventory, so it missed the non-obvious recombinations the human's 12-element matrix surfaced (clay-pot thermal mass for duty-cycle smoothing and battery extension, the low-temp/power-fail buzzer alarm circuit, and the battery depth-of-discharge sizing note — 60Ah at 77–92% DoD flagged borderline vs 100Ah at 46%), and its energy chain was checked once at selection rather than used as a screen over each candidate.
learning_signal: For design tasks, combinatorial recombination with an explicit element inventory and a per-recombination viability screen is both a completeness AND a filtering engine: the inventory is what makes non-obvious combinations (headlight-as-heater, thermal mass, alarm topology, battery reserve) reachable, and the per-concept screen (wattage vs heat load, battery Ah × outage with DoD reserve, recharge, safety chain, cost, serviceability) is what prevents volume from decaying into noise. The AI produced equivalent content because the constraint space was narrow enough to converge on; it lost the systematic coverage the style owns — the AI's own AAR concedes it never enumerated the local inventory and that battery-reserve reasoning arrived at selection, not as a screen.
suggested_improvement: Add a COMBINATORIAL IDEATION pass to HOW for design tasks: (1) enumerate ≥8 elements from the task context before proposing anything; (2) generate ≥10 recombinations with a visible trace; (3) screen each candidate on a fixed viability rubric (thermal/energy math, cost, safety, serviceability — computed per candidate, not asserted at selection); (4) record the selected configuration plus a reject log with the numeric reason for each discard. Require the WHY stage to budget the full energy chain (load → installed wattage margin → battery Ah × outage with depth-of-discharge reserve → recharge) before HOW begins, so the screen exists before ideation rather than being reconstructed at selection.

key_gap: Strict combinatorial style generated 18 recombinations of the TMU element space, of which most were not on the causal path (alarm-channel upgrades, desiccant, weekly calibration, dual-sensor averaging, ML anomaly detection); the true fix — remote probe into return air + 0.5°C hysteresis + 10-min confirmation delay, ≈$500 — was present as item 3 of 18 but unweighted, and selection by novelty/coverage picked a $12k cloud-monitoring bundle that blows the $3k budget and the 3-week timeline. The AI diagnosed first (falsified condensation, electronics, and compressor-cycle red herrings from the scenario data; supported door-draft transient on a fixed-threshold sensor), then screened every alternative against root cause + budget + timeline, selecting the ≈$500 fix with a ≤2%-alarm-nights 14-night verification target and a pre-specified escalation.
learning_signal: Recombination volume without diagnosis and without a constraint screen is derivative noise: when the element space is small and well-known (a TMU), recombinations mostly re-circulate non-causal variants, and novelty-based selection systematically favors the flashiest option (cloud, ML, replacement) over the working fix. The quality filter is the method's critical component — diagnosis (root cause evidenced, red herrings falsified) routes ideation to the causal path, and a budget/timeline/certification screen with explicit reject reasons kills the over-engineered options; the correct selection then falls out as the only candidate surviving both screens, with a numeric verification target and escalation rule.
suggested_improvement: Reinforce in the WHY gate and HOW stage: (1) keep diagnosis-before-ideation mandatory — every HOW alternative must cite the diagnosed causal element it acts on or be rejected (a causal-path check mirroring the human's absent filter); (2) add an explicit constraint screen to HOW alternatives — budget, timeline, certification — with a recorded reject reason per alternative (the human's failure to screen against budget is what let the $12k bundle win); (3) require verification with a numeric target and escalation rule in the decision packet for fix tasks (the AI's ≤2% / 14-night / else-reopen structure is the model to copy); (4) keep the reject log visible so generation volume is present but weighted.
